data.name: Marichi
data.gender_notes: Marichi is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Marichi is the name of the demon son of the Sun God, Surya. He is also known as Maricha and Marichi Makhadev. In Hindu mythology, Marichi is described as a powerful asura, a class of demons. He was a great sage, known for his wisdom and bravery. Marichi is said to have played a significant role in the churning of the ocean of milk, where he was rewarded with the horse, the celestial vehicle of Indra, the god of rain.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, power, and rebellion against the norm.
data.etymology: Marichi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the Sun God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marichi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Marichi is an essential figure in Hindu mythology, and his name holds significant cultural significance. He is a symbol of courage, strength, and wisdom, representing the power and complexity of the demonic forces that exist within the universe. The tale of Marichi's role in the churning of the ocean of milk is a well-known episode in Hindu mythology, and it illustrates the idea of all beings, divine or demonic, contributing to the creation of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: Marichi embodies the spiritual significance of knowledge, wisdom, and the power of will. He is a reminder that even the most early and seemingly evil beings can be redeemed and rewarded for their contributions. Additionally, Marichi's association with the Sun God represents the importance of the role of knowledge in spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Marichi is a name given to the demon son of Sage Kashyapa and his wife, Aditi. His name symbolizes intense heat and brilliance, reflecting his fiery nature. He is also known as the 'Shining One'.

historical_references.reference: Marichi is a sage mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Ramayana. He is the father of the demon Ravana and the sage Jatayu.
historical_references.context: Marichi is a sage and the father of two significant characters in Hindu mythology.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Marichi continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
